## Methodological finding (worth propagating to every future control set)

A control that *looks* like a perturbation may be a **symmetry of the statement**.
Swapping SHAPE B1's two withdrawal credentials on one side of the bridge only returns
**`Valid`**, correctly, because both are universally quantified and the base
validator's membership test is symmetric in them. Bridge controls must perturb
**asymmetrically**. Recorded in `WSC/Shaped/Probe/BridgeProbe4.lean` and
`WSC/SHAPE-BRIDGE.md` §7.1.

## HIGHEST-VALUE FOLLOW-ON identified by U1

**Restate `LR_BUDGET_base/minting/global/seize` against `ShapeBridge.XRun K` instead of
`appliedX_K.prop`.** The `XRun` form is the imported production bytecode plus the
audited `WSC/Prep/*` inputs function plus `cekExecuteProgram`, and nothing else — no
optimizer, no prep, available at *every* budget with no elaboration cost. Doing so
would (a) make the whole composition rest on the **kernel-checked** LEVEL-2 bridge
instead of a solver verdict, (b) remove `PropExecFaithful` from the trust base, and
(c) dissolve the Tier-A / Tier-B split, since the `XRun` right-hand side exists at
2500 / 3300 / 3800 / 4400 where no unshaped prep can be built. It is a rewrite of four
axiom statements plus the corresponding `bridge_*` uses; no new proving.
